newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan loses edge in exploiting technology.
newsitem.headline: Japan loses edge in exploiting technology.

text.p: After leading the world in using machines to boost productivity, Japan has fallen behind the United States and Germany in harnessing technological progress, the Trade Ministry said on Tuesday.

From 1975 to 1991, Japanese manufacturers, particularly in machinery-related areas, excelled at drawing the most productivity value from technological developments, the ministry said in an annual report.
But in the early nineties, an economic slump took the wind out of Japan's manufacturers and productivity took a turn for the worse, it said.
Meanwhile rivals in the United States and Germany gradually improved, with the United States in particular benefitting from huge innovation in the telecommunications sector, it said.

The ministry used a measure known as total factor productivity -- calculated using various economic data including real economic growth, asset distribution and workforce statistics -- to judge Japan's ability to exploit technology to increase productivity compared with other countries.

It found that Japan's service sector -- long weak in exploiting technological advances -- had fallen behind the United States and Germany. The gap with the United States is most marked in areas shaken up by aggressive deregulation, such as transport, communications and utilities sectors.

The report, blaming excessive regulation and high costs for the loss of productivity, said a more flexible and skilled workforce, as well as more basic research and better infrastructure, were needed to boost in productivity.

The report added that Japan needed to increase its attractiveness as a place to invest and said high labour costs, a heavy corporate tax burden and a lack of confidence about Japan's future as a market were turning away investors.
